general_information.Course Name English: Outcome-based Course Design in English Language Teaching
general_information.Description: _ This course provides English major students with an insight to Outcome-based education with the implementation of Project-based learning, which aims to develop a mindset of more student-centered approaches. _ Teaching methods/Pedagogical approaches: * Project-Based Learning * Problem-Based Learning * Task-Based Language Teaching * WebQuest-Based Learning * Flipped Classroom * Jigsaw Method * Tool-Based Pedagogy * Prototype-Based Learning * Constructivist Approach * Inquiry-Based Learning / Guided Inquiry / Scaffolded Inquiry * Discovery Learning * Collaborative Learning / Collaborative Brainstorming / Collaborative Inquiry * Case-Based Learning * Practice-Based Learning * Direct Instruction * Workshop-based Learning * Digital Literacy Pedagogy _ Teaching formats & activity types: Lecture + project work + AI-integrated learning activities
general_information.StudentTasks: _ Students must attend at least 80% of contact slots in order to be accepted to the final examination. _ Students are responsible for doing all exercises, and assignments given by instructor in class or at home by the due dates. _ Use laptops in class only for learning purposes.
general_information.Tools: _ Textbook _ Reference materials _ AI tools: * Bard (Gemini) * Canva / Canva AI * ChatGPT * Claude * Consensus * Curipod * Copilot * Eduaide * Elicit * Gamma * Kaiber * MagicForm AI * MagicSchool * Miro / Miro AI * Notion AI * Perplexity AI * Scite * SlidesAI * Tability * Tome AI
general_information.Note: Assessment scheme: 1) On-going assessment: - Assignment 1: 30% - Assignment 2: 30% - Assignment 3: 20% - Presentation and defense: 20% 2) Final result: 100% 3) Completion Criteria: Every on-going assessment >2, & Final Result >=5/10

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Analyze the principles and benefits of OBE in teaching English as a foreign language by comparing traditional and outcome-based approaches using AI research tools (NotebookLM, ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude) to synthesize educational literature and generate comparative frameworks.

Design the alignment between learning outcomes, instructional methods, and assessment strategies in an OBE framework utilizing AI-powered educational tools (MagicSchool AI, Eduaide.AI) to create coherent curriculum maps and alignment matrices.

Develop measurable and achievable learning outcomes for an EFL course using Bloom's taxonomy and SMART criteria with AI assistance (ChatGPT, Gemini) for language precision, clarity checking, and taxonomy alignment verification.

Evaluate the effectiveness of project-based learning activities in achieving specific learning outcomes within an OBE context by analyzing AI-generated data (adaptive learning platforms, Mentimeter analytics) and student engagement metrics

Create an authentic, outcome-aligned project proposal for EFL learners, including timeline, resources, and success criteria using AI content creation tools (MagicSchool AI, Canva AI) for multimedia resources and differentiated materials

Apply formative and summative assessment principles to design assessment tools that measure learning outcome achievement leveraging AI assessment generators and automated rubric creators for efficient, fair evaluation systems

Construct detailed rubrics with clear performance criteria and proficiency levels for project-based assessments using AI-powered rubric generators and natural language processing tools for precise criterion definition

Demonstrate effective collaboration skills by contributing meaningfully to group project implementation and peer feedback processes facilitated by AI collaboration platforms (Google Workspace AI, Microsoft Copilot) for enhanced communication and project management
Evaluate the ethical implications and limitations of AI tools in educational settings by analyzing bias, privacy, and pedagogical effectiveness in EFL contexts
Apply AI translation and language processing tools to develop inclusive, multilingual educational resources for diverse EFL classroom environments

assessments.Question Type: Description:In this assignment, students will design Course Learning Outcomes (CLOs) for an English as a Foreign Language (EFL) course. This task will require students to apply the principles of Outcome-Based Education (OBE) and understand the significance of basing education on outcomes. Students will create CLOs that reflect the essential skills and competencies students should acquire by the end of the course. Students should consider integrating the cognitive domains of learning from Bloom’s Taxonomy.Context:Imagine you are part of a team of educational consultants who have been hired by a prestigious language institute to revamp their English as a Foreign Language (EFL) program. The institute’s goal is to offer a cutting-edge course that not only enhances students' language skills but also prepares them to thrive in an increasingly globalized world. To achieve this, the institute has decided to adopt an Outcome-Based Education (OBE) approach, ensuring that every aspect of the course is aligned with clearly defined learning outcomes.Step-by-step guidelines:Identify the Course ObjectivesIdentify Key OutcomesFormulate Your CLOs Using Bloom’s Taxonomy as a GuidelineEnsure CLOs Are SMART
assessments.Grading Guide: Group work (3-4 people/ a group) with a clear task delegation

assessments.Question Type: Description:In this assignment, students will design a WebQuests as part of a Project-Based Learning (PBL) approach. The WebQuests will serve as a guide for students to complete a project based on the Course Learning Outcomes (CLOs) students have designed in the previous assignment. This WebQuests should include a clear project idea, a driving question, steps for project implementation, useful resources, and a conclusion with a feedback form.Design a webquest for a project of the course in Assignment 1 including: - the project idea and artifacts - a driving question - task and process of the project implementation (steps) - useful sources for students to work on the project - a conclusion with a feedback form- at least one AI tool during the creation of your WebQuest.
assessments.Grading Guide: Group work (3-4 people/ a group) with a clear task delegation

assessments.Question Type: Description:In this assignment, students are required to construct a rubric or rubrics to grade the artifacts produced in Assignment 2. This will involve applying the principles of assessment for Project-Based Learning (PBL), including considerations for holistic versus analytical rubrics, as well as incorporating self-evaluation and peer-evaluation.Step-by-Step Guidelines:Review the WebQuest and CLOsDecide on the Type of Rubric (Holistic vs. Analytical)Identify Key Assessment CriteriaDefine Performance LevelsConstruct the RubricReview and Refine the RubricSubmit the Rubric and Group Report
assessments.Grading Guide: Group work (3-4 people/ a group) with a clear task delegation
assessments.Note: The evaluation page on the webquest of assignment 2

assessments.Duration: Presentation: 15 minutes each group Defense: 3 minutes each person
assessments.Question Type: Description:In this final task, students will deliver a presentation on the alignment of the project you designed in Assignment 2, the rubric(s) they constructed in Assignment 3, and the Course Learning Outcomes (CLOs) established in Assignment 1. This presentation is a critical part of your course, as it demonstrates your understanding of how these elements work together to achieve effective learning outcomes.Tasks:Presentation (15 minutes): Collaborate with your group members to prepare a 15-minute presentation. Ensure that your presentation clearly explains how the project, rubric(s), and CLOs are aligned. Clearly state which AI tools were used in preparing the slides, visuals, or data comparisons.Defense (3 minutes):Following the presentation, each group member will participate in a 3-minute defense. During this defense, you will be asked to respond to at least one question related to the presentation. These questions may cover any aspect of the project, rubric(s), or CLOs, and your ability to defend your choices will be critical to your assessment.
assessments.No Question: At least 1 question for each member to defend
assessments.Grading Guide: Group work (3-4 people/ a group) with a clear task delegation

schedule.Topic: Course Introduction + Introduction to the course objectives an outcomes
schedule.Student's Tasks: _ Class discussion, group division

schedule.Topic: Introduction to EFL
schedule.Student's Tasks: _Analyze how EFL is defined and implemented in different contexts by using AI search assistants (e.g., Perplexity, Scite, ChatGPT with browsing) to gather definitions and compare key features of EFL vs. ESL.

schedule.Topic: OUTCOME-BASED EDUCATION: + Introduction to OBE +What are outcomes?
schedule.Student's Tasks: _Generate definitions, examples, and key components of learning outcomes by interacting with AI tools (e.g., ChatGPT, You.com, or Consensus.app).

schedule.Topic: OUTCOME-BASED EDUCATION: +What are outcomes? (cont.) + What does it mean to base education on outcomes?
schedule.Student's Tasks: _Compare how different AI tools (e.g., ChatGPT, Perplexity, Scite) define the “outcome-based approach” and identify common elements.

schedule.Topic: OUTCOME-BASED EDUCATION: +4 stages on OBE and how they are aligned
schedule.Student's Tasks: _Map the 4 stages of OBE (i.e., 1) Intended Learning Outcomes, 2) Curriculum and Delivery, 3) Assessment, 4) Evaluation & Feedback) using an AI-supported concept mapping tool (e.g., Miro AI, Whimsical AI, or Lucidchart AI).

schedule.Topic: OUTCOME-BASED EDUCATION: +4 key issues in OBE
schedule.Student's Tasks: _Evaluate the 4 key issues in OBE (e.g., outcome clarity, alignment, assessment validity, and learner-centeredness) by using AI tools to gather and contrast expert perspectives, then reflect critically on their impact in the EFL context.

schedule.Topic: OUTCOME-BASED EDUCATION - Stage 1: + Bloom's 3 learning domains
schedule.Student's Tasks: _Classify learning outcomes into Bloom’s 3 domains (Cognitive, Affective, Psychomotor) using AI assistance.

schedule.Topic: OUTCOME-BASED EDUCATION - Stage 1: + Different levels of outcomes
schedule.Student's Tasks: _Differentiate between various levels of outcomes (Program Learning Outcomes – PLOs, Course Learning Outcomes – CLOs, and Session/Unit-level Outcomes – SLOs or ULOs) using AI-assisted comparison tools.

schedule.Topic: OUTCOME-BASED EDUCATION: +Mapping PLOs and CLOs
schedule.Student's Tasks: _Map sample Course Learning Outcomes (CLOs) to relevant Program Learning Outcomes (PLOs) using AI tools and evaluate their alignment.

schedule.Topic: OUTCOME-BASED EDUCATION: +Mapping PLOs and CLOs +Practice Introduction and guidance to assignment 2
schedule.Student's Tasks: _Apply AI tools to complete a hands-on PLO–CLO mapping task, followed by a guided introduction to Assignment 2.

schedule.Topic: OUTCOME-BASED EDUCATION: + Bloom's taxonomy of cognitive domain
schedule.Student's Tasks: _Analyze the six levels of Bloom’s cognitive domain (Remember, Understand, Apply, Analyze, Evaluate, Create) and use AI tools to construct or revise learning outcomes according to each level.

schedule.Topic: OUTCOME-BASED EDUCATION: + Bloom's taxonomy of cognitive domain
schedule.Student's Tasks: _Distinguish between the six levels of the cognitive domain and construct level-specific learning outcomes using AI support.

schedule.Topic: OUTCOME-BASED EDUCATION: + Bloom's taxonomy of cognitive domain (cont.) +Practice writing CLOs
schedule.Student's Tasks: _Compose and refine Course Learning Outcomes (CLOs) that align with Bloom’s cognitive levels using AI tools for brainstorming, evaluation, and improvement.

schedule.Topic: OUTCOME-BASED EDUCATION: +Practice writing CLOs
schedule.Student's Tasks: _Draft, revise, and evaluate CLOs for a specific EFL course using AI support.

schedule.Topic: OUTCOME-BASED EDUCATION - Stage 1 +Lesson learning outcomes
schedule.Student's Tasks: _Construct well-aligned lesson-level learning outcomes for an EFL lesson using AI tools to support Bloom-level identification, verb selection, and outcome formulation.

schedule.Topic: OUTCOME-BASED EDUCATION - Stage 1 +Designing LOs +Attaining LOs
schedule.Student's Tasks: _Design effective learning outcomes for a short EFL course and evaluate strategies to help students attain them using AI-supported planning.

schedule.Topic: OUTCOME-BASED EDUCATION - Stage 2 +Teacher-centered approach vs. Student-centered approach
schedule.Student's Tasks: _Compare the features, advantages, and drawbacks of teacher-centered vs. student-centered approaches, and evaluate which is more aligned with OBE principles, using AI tools to explore practical examples.

schedule.Topic: OUTCOME-BASED EDUCATION - Stage 2 +Teacher-centered approach vs. Student-centered approach
schedule.Student's Tasks: _Analyze the characteristics of teacher-centered and student-centered approaches, and evaluate their relevance to OBE delivery using AI-supported research and comparison tools.

schedule.Topic: PROJECT-BASED LEARNING: PBL introduction Introduction and guidance to assignment 2
schedule.Student's Tasks: _ Explore a PBL case study using ChatGPT or Bard _ Analyze the key components of PBL (driving question, product, assessment) _ Discuss in pairs the benefits of PBL in OBE context.

schedule.Topic: PROJECT-BASED LEARNING: PBL introduction Introduction and guidance to assignment 2 (cont.)
schedule.Student's Tasks: _ Use Tome AI or Canva AI to create a visual mindmap of PBL components and how they align with CLOs and assessment strategies in OBE; _ Share mindmap in groups for peer feedback.

schedule.Topic: PROJECT-BASED LEARNING: The role of PBL in OBE submission of assignment 1
schedule.Student's Tasks: _ Explore PBL in OBE by prompting ChatGPT or Gemini. _ Summarize the output and highlight keywords using Tome AI or Notion AI

schedule.Topic: PROJECT-BASED LEARNING: The role of PBL in OBE
schedule.Student's Tasks: _ Analyze a sample PBL scenario using Eduaide.ai. _ Use Canva AI or SlidesAI, create a short pitch deck that outlines the key components of a project (goal, task, assessment, AI support). _ Reflect in small groups on how AI helped understanding.

schedule.Topic: PROJECT-BASED LEARNING: The Lingo of PBL
schedule.Student's Tasks: _ Identify and define key PBL terms (e.g., Anchor, Artifact, Driving Question). _ ChatGPT or Claude to paraphrase and generate examples in an EFL context.

schedule.Topic: PROJECT-BASED LEARNING: The Lingo of PBL (cont.)
schedule.Student's Tasks: _ Create visual mind maps of PBL terminology using Canva AI, including AI-generated examples for each term to illustrate meaning.

schedule.Topic: PROJECT-BASED LEARNING: The Lingo of PBL (cont.)
schedule.Student's Tasks: _ Compare PBL terms across real-world case studies by asking AI tools to explain how each term is realized in classroom projects (e.g., “What is an artifact in a grade 10 writing project?”).

schedule.Topic: PROJECT-BASED LEARNING: The Lingo of PBL (cont.)
schedule.Student's Tasks: _ Evaluate the effectiveness of various PBL terms in actual lesson design by feeding sample lesson plans into Eduaide.ai _ Identify how terms like “authentic achievement” or “student voice” are reflected.

schedule.Topic: PROJECT-BASED LEARNING: PBL vs. Traditional project assignments
schedule.Student's Tasks: _ Compare the characteristics of PBL vs. traditional projects using ChatGPT or Claude to generate side-by-side comparisons based on specific criteria (e.g., assessment, student role, collaboration, authenticity).

schedule.Topic: PROJECT-BASED LEARNING: PBL vs. Traditional project assignments (cont.)
schedule.Student's Tasks: _ Evaluate a sample traditional project and a sample PBL task using Eduaide.ai or ChatGPT, focusing on how each aligns with OBE and 21st-century skills (authenticity, student voice, collaboration, etc.). _ Propose enhancements using AI to convert the traditional one into a PBL-aligned version.

schedule.Topic: PROJECT-BASED LEARNING: +How does PBL fit into the curriculum
schedule.Student's Tasks: _ Analyze an existing EFL course syllabus using ChatGPT or Eduaide.ai to identify whether and how PBL elements are present. _Propose how PBL could be better aligned with the course’s LOs and assessments.

schedule.Topic: PROJECT-BASED LEARNING: +Challenges for teachers in PBL
schedule.Student's Tasks: _ Identify and evaluate common challenges teachers face when implementing PBL in EFL contexts using GenAI tools like Perplexity AI or ChatGPT. _ Generate AI-assisted suggestions for overcoming these challenges.

schedule.Topic: PROJECT-BASED LEARNING: +Specific Processes for Investigation and Research
schedule.Student's Tasks: _ Generate driving questions for an EFL project by using ChatGPT or Curipod to brainstorm ideas based on chosen themes. _Refine those into SMART sub-questions using tools like Perplexity AI or elicit.org.

schedule.Topic: PROJECT-BASED LEARNING: +Specific Processes for Investigation and Research (cont.)
schedule.Student's Tasks: _ Use Consensus.app or elicit.org to search for empirical evidence related to one of the driving questions. _ Compare the results across platforms, select relevant findings.

schedule.Topic: PROJECT-BASED LEARNING: Designing PBL projects: pre-planning questions
schedule.Student's Tasks: _ Brainstorm pre-planning questions for a PBL project (e.g., learner needs, context, topic suitability) using ChatGPT and Canva Magic Write. _ Use AI to generate a broad range of possible questions, then prioritize the top 5 questions using a shared Miro board.

schedule.Topic: PROJECT-BASED LEARNING: Designing PBL projects: pre-planning questions (cont.)
schedule.Student's Tasks: _ Refine their top 5 pre-planning questions by testing them against OBE-aligned learning outcomes _ Use Perplexity AI and elicit.org to check if their questions can be connected to assessable, observable LOs.

schedule.Topic: PROJECT-BASED LEARNING: Designing PBL projects: Steps in a PBL Instructional Project: steps 1,2,3
schedule.Student's Tasks: _ Brainstorm team project ideas and develop a basic project outline using ChatGPT (to generate prompts and goals) _ Use Tome AI to design a collaborative visual storyboard outlining steps 1–3 (team planning, initial research, artifact idea).

schedule.Topic: PROJECT-BASED LEARNING: Designing PBL projects: Steps in a PBL Instructional Project: steps 1,2,3 (cont.)
schedule.Student's Tasks: _ Use Canva AI Whiteboard to finalize and co-edit team’s plan with role division, timeline, and preliminary driving question. _ Cross-check with Eduaide.ai to validate alignment with OBE elements.

schedule.Topic: PROJECT-BASED LEARNING: Designing PBL projects: Steps in a PBL Instructional Project: steps 4,5,6
schedule.Student's Tasks: _ Revise prototype artifacts and storyboards using ChatGPT (to generate updated content) và Gamma.app _ Kaiber hoặc Canva AI Video to draft ideas for final presentation (video/art-based).

schedule.Topic: PROJECT-BASED LEARNING: Designing PBL projects: Steps in a PBL Instructional Project: steps 4,5,6 (cont.)
schedule.Student's Tasks: _ Finalize and publish artifacts on Padlet, Notion, hoặc Google Sites. _ Use Eduaide.ai to generate reflection questions on project-based learning process and AI collaboration.

schedule.Topic: PROJECT-BASED LEARNING: Instructional technology in PBL - a webquest
schedule.Student's Tasks: _ Explore what WebQuests are by analyzing examples (e.g., Civil War WebQuest). _ Use Google Sites to identify one existing WebQuest and discuss its structure and purpose.

schedule.Topic: PROJECT-BASED LEARNING: Instructional technology in PBL - a webquest (cont.)
schedule.Student's Tasks: _ Identify and analyze key components of a WebQuest (Introduction, Task, Process, Resources, Evaluation, Conclusion). _ Evaluate two existing WebQuests using a rubric (Box 4.3 as reference).

schedule.Topic: PROJECT-BASED LEARNING: Instructional technology in PBL - a webquest (cont.)
schedule.Student's Tasks: _ Draft their own WebQuest scenario including a driving question. _ Use AI tools (e.g., ChatGPT or Claude) to generate example tasks or comprehension questions for selected web resources.

schedule.Topic: PROJECT-BASED LEARNING: Instructional technology in PBL - a webquest (cont.)
schedule.Student's Tasks: _ Modify their WebQuest to differentiate for varied learner profiles (e.g., English proficiency levels). _ Publish WebQuest on Google Sites, and share it with peers for feedback.

schedule.Topic: PROJECT-BASED LEARNING: Instructional technology in PBL - Useful softwares and devices
schedule.Student's Tasks: _ Explore and categorize at least 5 AI or EdTech tools by their pedagogical function. _ Use a tool like MindMeister or Miro AI to visually map functions and limitations.

schedule.Topic: PROJECT-BASED LEARNING: Instructional technology in PBL - Useful softwares and devices (cont.)
schedule.Student's Tasks: _ Evaluate the effectiveness of two AI tools (e.g., Eduaide.ai vs. Canva Magic Write) for different PBL phases.

schedule.Topic: Introduction and guidance to assignment 3 PROJECT-BASED LEARNING: Assessment for PBL,holistic rubrics vs. analytical rubrics
schedule.Student's Tasks: _ Compare a holistic rubric and an analytical rubric generated by Eduaide.ai or Rubricator.ai based on a sample EFL project. _ Highlight strengths, limitations, and alignment with OBE principles.

schedule.Topic: Introduction and guidance to assignment 3 PROJECT-BASED LEARNING: Assessment for PBL,holistic rubrics vs. analytical rubrics (cont.)
schedule.Student's Tasks: _ Design their own rubric (either holistic or analytical) for their EFL project using ChatGPT or Eduaide.ai, _ Peer-review rubrics using a reflection form based on rubric quality indicators (validity, clarity, AI ethics).

schedule.Topic: PROJECT-BASED LEARNING: Assessment for PBL: developing rubrics
schedule.Student's Tasks: _ Draft a preliminary rubric (analytic or holistic) for their PBL project using Eduaide.ai or Formative AI Rubric Builder - Revise it by comparing with rubrics retrieved from ChatGPT or Rubricator.ai.

schedule.Topic: PROJECT-BASED LEARNING: Assessment for PBL: developing rubrics (cont.)
schedule.Student's Tasks: _ Collaborate in teams to finalize their rubrics using ChatGPT and peer feedback. _ Evaluate one team’s rubric using an AI bias checklist and propose edits to improve clarity and fairness.

schedule.Topic: PROJECT-BASED LEARNING: Assessment for PBL, self-evaluation and peer-evaluation submission of assignment 2
schedule.Student's Tasks: _ Explore and critique two AI-supported self-assessment tools (e.g., Tability, Eduaide.ai Self-reflection generator) _ Reflect on how AI feedback compares with their self-perception.

schedule.Topic: PROJECT-BASED LEARNING: Assessment for PBL, self-evaluation and peer-evaluation
schedule.Student's Tasks: _ Collaborate in small groups to co-create peer-evaluation forms with the help of Google Forms + AI tools like MagicForm AI or Gemini. _ Compare traditional rubrics with AI-suggested questions.

schedule.Topic: One sample ESL project review submission of assignment 3
schedule.Student's Tasks: _ Analyze a sample ESL PBL product (e.g., a podcast, lesson plan, or classroom video) using ChatGPT or Claude.ai to generate guided critiques based on previously learned rubric criteria.

schedule.Topic: One sample ESL project review (cont.)
schedule.Student's Tasks: _ Generate an evaluation report of the same sample project using Notion AI or Eduaide.ai to structure findings. _ Compare their AI-supported report with other groups’ versions to spot inconsistencies or biases.
